feature.title: Phone and iPad reader: library, outline, chapter reader, reading settings
feature.problem: Courses can only be read on the desktop web app, whose sidebar, panels and notes do not fit a phone. The owner wants to read a course on an iPhone or iPad the way they read a book: large, calm text, one tap to resume where they stopped, and nothing else on screen. The Phase 0 spike proved the stack (react-native-web at /m/, the shared API layer, the tutor stream); this phase builds the reading itself from the approved design canvas https://claude.ai/artifact/LUdrDTLccSWPURFiLgHjYS.
nonGoals: The tutor sheet, paragraph asking and docked tutor pane: Phase 3. The spike's tutor box is removed from the library screen.
End-of-chapter quizzes and Flowmovie/Mermaid diagrams: Phase 2. A chapter's diagrams and questions are not shown yet.
Offline reading, install manifest and service worker: Phase 4.
Notes, sources, creating courses and projects: never in the reader.

states.loading: Title and six text-line skeletons at reading width; the top bar and progress bar are already in place.
states.empty: This chapter is still being written. Pick another from the outline. [Open outline]

components.why: a handful of courses; every row renders at once, so a virtualised list buys nothing and complicates scroll restoration
the peak of this screen is resuming; the server already records the last opened chapter per course
components.rejected: a 'recent' section built from local history (wrong on a second device)

components.control: markdown-it tokens rendered by our own React Native blocks (mobile/src/markdown/)
components.why: we control typography, the Key idea callout and code scrolling exactly, with no native-only dependencies; markdown-it already ships in the tree
components.rejected: react-native-markdown-display (pulls native-only packages and its own styling model)

components.why: iPad Split View and Slide Over change the window, not the device; the width is the only honest signal

components.control: Hand-written router over the History API (mobile/src/router.ts, four routes)
components.why: four routes, no nested layouts, back button and deep links are all it needs; avoids a second router package in the bundle
components.rejected: TanStack Router (its code-based tree and devtools are built around the desktop shell) and React Navigation (native-first, heavy on web)

components.control: Scroll position saved per chapter on this device
components.why: the peak of resuming is landing on the paragraph, not the top of the chapter
components.rejected: server-side scroll position (no endpoint, and it would fight across devices)

components.control: Segmented buttons (aria-pressed) and a range input
components.why: three or two mutually exclusive options read faster as visible choices than behind a menu, and each applies on change

components.control: Zustand store persisted to localStorage, wrapped in try/catch
components.why: settings are per device and synchronous, and zustand is already a dependency
components.rejected: a server endpoint (no reason for a phone's font size to follow you to the desktop)
